Hi Aisha —

Thanks for the clear list. Taking this in two parts: legal/contracting and technical operations. Quick summary up front: Redwood can execute the UK Addendum (we route that through our legal team) and we also provide technical and organizational safeguards to operate under SCCs where customers prefer that path.

Action plan I propose:
1) Legal: Laura will confirm signing path for the UK Addendum and provide a DocuSign link if needed (we can do either attachment or DocuSign).
2) Subprocessors: I'll attach our current export of the subprocessor register (CSV) and flag which processors handle key material.
3) Technical safeguards: Marissa will follow up with a brief TIA checklist mapping (KV cache locations, onshore fallback, encryption-in-transit and at rest, HSM/KMS boundaries).
4) Timeline: initial packet back to you by Thu EOD, and a follow-up call Friday to close open items if that works.

For transparency: we operate a split approach — for EU residency customers we can (a) support SCCs + technical mitigations (prefix caching, regional routing, controlled KV egress), or (b) execute the UK Addendum/IDTA if you prefer a contract-based path for UK-data. The technical differences are mostly around where KV cache is persisted and which regions are allowed to process request metadata.

I'm attaching our internal TIA checklist (living doc) so you can see the exact artifacts we'll provide.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Head, Trust & Privacy Operations

Hi Samir / Aisha —

Quick legal note before the call: Redwood is able to sign the UK Addendum via DocuSign. We typically attach the signed Addendum to our master DPA and can also record the effective date in the contract metadata. If Mediflow prefers to rely on SCCs + mitigations instead, we'll include a short scheduling clause and operational artifacts in the TIA packet.

On the HSM/KMS point: we (Redwood) use a customer-key option for enterprise Private deployments; for Hosted customers we manage encryption keys using a cloud KMS (AWS KMS / GCP KMS depending on region). We do not share HSM keys with third-party subprocessors — any HSM-backed key management is operated by Redwood in those scenarios and is regional. Laura can confirm vendor specifics during the call.

I'll prepare a short legal summary of the signing path and a DocuSign link (I'll share it in the call notes).

Regards,
